answer: Sybil resistance for AI agents relies on a deposit mechanism. Each agent must lock a substantial economic stake in a secure, audited vault. This capital serves as a bond against malicious action. The cost to acquire and maintain these stakes makes identity creation expensive, costing an attacker direct capital proportional to the desired number of fake identities. A monitoring falcon quickly identifies stake-backed agents exhibiting abnormal behavior, while a network zephyr confirms stake validity.
